title: Chicago CTA monthly rail boardings
brief: Revision 2 applies the owner's decisions of 2026-11-08. Entrants forecast how many rail boardings CTA will report for a coming calendar month, from the CTA 'Daily Boarding Totals' table on the City of Chicago Data Portal (6iiy-9s97). It is keyless and runs from 2001 to 2026-08-31. Forecasts lock before the month starts. Rounds resolve on the first daily snapshot that holds every day of the month, which has taken 40 to 150 days. Decided: rail only. The ranked zero point is the calendar-aware same-month-last-year reference with a 3-month trend and a 12-month RMS spread, written as yoy(k=3, calendar=true, spread=rms12) (formerly 'cal_yoy3'). January and February 2027 run as unscored pilot rounds, and the pilot may archive privately. For maintainers: nothing is scored until you accept the reading of the City's Data Terms of Use and its indemnity clause, because the arena connects no source without explicit written permission. The first scored lock is Sun 2027-02-28, for March 2027, if that acceptance has arrived by then.
question: How many rail boardings will CTA report for the target calendar month, summing rail_boardings over every service_date of that month in the CTA 'Ridership - Daily Boarding Totals' dataset, read from the resolution snapshot?

source.publisher: Chicago Transit Authority (data owner), published on the City of Chicago Data Portal (data.cityofchicago.org, Tyler/Socrata). Dataset 'CTA - Ridership - Daily Boarding Totals', 6iiy-9s97, attribution 'Chicago Transit Authority', licence field 'See Terms of Use' [verified 2026-11-09T01:11:02Z].
source.access: Socrata SODA endpoint https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/6iiy-9s97.json. No key and no token [verified: three unauthenticated requests returned HTTP 200 on 2026-11-09 between 01:11Z and 01:18Z; the full 2016-to-date pull of 3,896 rows took 2.9 s]. Daily fetch at 14:00 UTC: GET .../resource/6iiy-9s97.json?$where=service_date >= '<fetch day - 900 days>'&$order=service_date&$limit=5000. That is about 900 rows and 110 KB. A second, small request records batch timing: $select=date_trunc_ym(service_date) as m, date_trunc_ymd(to_floating_timestamp(:created_at,'America/Chicago')) as c, count(*) as n&$group=m,c. Bodies are written as served to sources/cta_daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json, with provenance in sources/manifest.json (ssa/provenance.py). The archive is the resolution source, because the endpoint cannot be read as of a past date and CTA re-publishes whole years: every 2024 row has :created_at 2025-04-29. The refresh runs on datacenter runners. The data host answered 200 from here. www.chicago.gov, where the terms live, returned 403 to an honest user agent (01:11:20Z), so a portal-side block is possible. A 403 on the first pilot day means a local courier (lesson 3). Not used: the doc's TNP trips dataset. A grouped monthly count over 6dvr-xwnh did not finish within 3 minutes (2026-11-09T01:12Z), so any TNP adapter must query one bounded month at a time.
source.archive_policy: Use: allowed, inferred. Automated retrieval: not addressed. Redistribution: allowed with a disclaimer, inferred. Evidence: (a) The City of Chicago 'Data Terms of Use', read from the Wayback copy of 2026-10-28, because the live page returned 403. 'USE OF DATA': 'The City may require a user of this data to terminate any and all display, distribution or other use of any or all of the data provided at this website for any reason'. Anyone 'providing any software application, or other secondary or derivative application using data supplied at this website' must show the City's disclaimer ('This site provides applications using data that has been modified for use from its original source, www.cityofchicago.org ...') and 'Comply with any additional Terms of Use set forth by the City agency or department providing data'. 'RESERVATION OF RIGHTS': the City may claim IP and 'will so indicate on the webpage'. No such notice is on 6iiy-9s97. 'INDEMNITY': 'any user of the data ... shall indemnify and hold harmless the City from any claim ... that arises directly or indirectly ... from that user's use of this data', with a duty to defend [verified text]. (b) There is no clause on bots, scraping or API retrieval. The portal publishes the SODA API. (c) CTA, the 'agency providing data', may have additional terms. None were checked [unverified]. Reading: distribution is contemplated (the City may 'terminate ... distribution'), so redistribution with the disclaimer is a reasonable inference, but lesson 1 asks for terms that clearly allow it. The indemnity duty falls on SSA as a user. Proposed inventory row (owner decision, rev 2): 'permission-needed', proposed for maintainers and not granted. Nothing is scored, and no public archive is published, until maintainers accept this reading and the indemnity clause, because the arena connects no source without explicit written permission. The pilot may archive privately. If they accept, the row becomes 'approved' with the conditions: show the City disclaimer on the round page, and cite 'Chicago Transit Authority, CTA - Ridership - Daily Boarding Totals (6iiy-9s97), City of Chicago Data Portal' with the snapshot date. The agent does not grant it. Task for a person, once a maintainer says go (nobody sends anything before that): (1) In an ordinary browser, open https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/narr/foia/data_disclaimer.html, which returned 403 here. Confirm it matches the Wayback text quoted above, and save it with its date. (2) Look on transitchicago.com for any CTA terms covering ridership data, the 'additional Terms of Use' the City's terms point to, and record what is found. (3) Send the following message through the dataset page's 'Contact Dataset Owner' form, or to CTA's open-data contact. Message: 'We run a non-commercial public research benchmark. We would fetch CTA Daily Boarding Totals (6iiy-9s97) once a day through the SODA API and publish the unmodified daily copies with hashes, alongside the City's disclaimer. Is that consistent with the Data Portal Terms of Use and any CTA terms?'

target.population: Every rail boarding CTA reports for its whole service area, which includes neighbouring municipalities (the doc). rail_boardings counts entries plus cross-platform transfers, so it is a system boarding count, not a station-entry sum (the doc's transit definitions). Bus is excluded from this number and is the runner-up second cell.
target.window: Calendar month by CTA service_date. A service date is CTA's operating day, not midnight to midnight.
target.calculation: Sum of rail_boardings over the service_date rows of the target month in the resolution snapshot. All days must be present, one row per date (unique key service_date). bus + rail_boardings = total_rides is logged as a check. It held for all 3,896 rows since 2016 [verified].
target.unit: Rail boardings per calendar month (about 9.5 to 13.6 million over the last 12 months)

lock: 23:59 America/Chicago on the last day of the month before the target month (the doc: 'For monthly questions, close before 00:00 America/Chicago on the first target day'), stored in UTC. There is no publisher calendar, so the round text says that SSA sets and resolves the metric (docs/sources.md §1.1). At lock the newest complete month is usually M-3 or M-4. For example, on 2026-11-09 the newest day was 2026-08-31, 70 days back. First pilot lock: Thu 2026-12-31 23:59 CT, for January 2027. Rev 2 (G3): January and February 2027 (locks Thu 2026-12-31 and Sun 2027-01-31) run as unscored pilot rounds, archived privately. The first scored lock is Sun 2027-02-28 23:59 CT, for March 2027, and only once maintainers have accepted the rights reading (see source). That needs the adapter on main with the daily refresh running by Thu 2026-12-10, which leaves about 4.5 weeks for owner approval, the PR to dev, review and the separate dev-to-main merge, then 3 weeks for participants (lesson 7). The pilot rounds are posted marked unscored. The go/no-go (see resolution) is recorded before the March 2027 round's lock if the September and October 2026 batches have both landed and settled by then, and otherwise before that round resolves. If main is reached later, each pilot and scored lock moves one month later. A December 2026 round (lock Mon 2026-11-30) is too tight to post.
baseline: Ranked zero point (owner decision, rev 2): calendar-aware seasonal naive with a trend. It is written as the parameterised reference yoy(k=3, calendar=true, spread=rms12) (rev 1 called it 'cal_yoy3'). This is the same family the Texas card uses with k=0, calendar=false. This is the doc's 'seasonal calendar-aware forecast built from the latest published complete weeks available at lock, with a trend adjustment defined in advance'. All inputs come from the lock capture. (1) Day-type counts for the target month: W (weekday), A (Saturday), U (Sunday or holiday). The holidays are CTA's six observed ones: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas, on their observed dates (2026-07-03 was coded U). That matches every non-standard coding since 2022 [verified]. (2) Base = sum over W, A and U of (days of that type in M) x (mean rail_boardings per day of that type in M-12). (3) Trend = sum of the three newest complete months L, L-1, L-2 in the capture, divided by the same three months a year earlier. If L is older than M-5, the round is not posted. Reference = base x trend. Spread: sd = reference x RMS of the same rule's percent errors over the 12 most recent target months complete in the capture, each recomputed with the same L offset. Shown, not ranked: plain seasonal naive (M-12's total) and the calendar-aware base without the trend, each spread the same way. Measured on 38 target months, 2023-07 to 2026-08 (modern backfill, not first prints), MAPE: reference 3.11% with L = M-3 (median 2.95, max 8.90), 3.61% with L = M-4. Plain seasonal naive 7.41%, calendar base 7.25%. Last 12 months of reference error, with L = M-3: Sep 2025 -0.7%, Oct +2.0, Nov +4.7, Dec +5.7, Jan 2026 +7.4, Feb 0.0, Mar +3.0, Apr +2.9, May +2.0, Jun +0.8, Jul +0.4, Aug +1.7. It ran high in 10 of 12 months, because the trend lags a slowing recovery. The worst months are the winter holidays and a cold January.
resolution: The first daily snapshot, at 14:00 UTC, that holds all service dates of the target month. The value is that snapshot's sum, and later re-publications never change it. This replaces the doc's fixed 'day 75'. Measured month-end-to-posting lag over Jan 2025 to Aug 2026: 150, 122, 91, 61, 87, 57, 53, 68, 50, 90, 47, 79, 48, 48, 45, 56, 40, 44, 59, 58 days. Months have posted out of order (Nov 2025 on 2026-01-16, before Oct 2025 on 01-29). A fixed day 75 would have missed 6 of these 20 months [verified from :created_at]. The doc's 40 to 59 days covers Mar to Aug 2026 only. Expected: January 2027 resolves in mid to late March 2027. Cap: if the month is not complete by day 100 after month end, the round is void. Pilot (rev 2: two unscored rounds, January and February 2027, archived privately): the daily snapshots must see the Sep and Oct 2026 batches arrive, and each month's sum must hold within 0.1% over the 14 daily snapshots after it first appears. A maintainer records go or no-go before January 2027 resolves. No-go: the March 2027 round also runs unscored (announced before its lock), and a new revision sets a waiting period after first appearance.
missing_data_policy: (1) A month that is partly present (some days missing) is not complete and does not resolve. If it is still partial at day 100, the round is void. (2) A date coded with an unexpected day_type, or any row where bus + rail_boardings differs from total_rides, holds the round for maintainer review before it resolves. (3) A day below 30% of the median for its day type over the prior 28 days is flagged and kept, because real shocks such as a blizzard or a system shutdown count. It is not dropped. (4) At lock: if M-12 is missing a day, or L is older than M-5, the round is not posted. (5) Failed daily fetches are recorded, never back-filled. (6) Backtests use today's backfill, which includes the 2025-04-29 re-publication of 2024, and are labelled that way.
scoring: SSA topline scoring of a predictive distribution over the monthly count (continuous_normal, mean and sd or quantiles), scored with CRPS. Skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant) / CRPS(yoy(k=3, calendar=true, spread=rms12)). Check that submitting the reference scores about 0. Over 2025-01 to 2026-08 (20 months), an entrant who submits the reference mean and only rescales the sd gains +0.0%, and the 90% interval covers 17 of 20. Over the longer 2023-07 to 2026-08 window, rescaling gains +7.9% at k 0.55 (L = M-3) and +11.0% (L = M-4). The 2023 recovery months inflate the 12-month RMS, so the reference runs wide when ridership is trending. Mean CRPS of the reference is 2.28% of the monthly level over 2025-26, against 4.28% for plain seasonal naive [verified computation]. Movement check (arena scoring.noise_floor on the calendar-adjusted YoY index, last 20 months): m = 2.04, s = 2.26. There is movement beyond noise, so the series is scoreable. Bus ran the same way: reference MAPE 3.36% against 8.72% for seasonal naive.

[owner input] The section carries 'Contributor: xiaoyuyan2028@u.northwestern.edu' and no 'Contact:' line. That person is not in the overview's contributor list, and the Contacts table does not list the section. The doc recommends piloting five datasets. It proposes event profiles (Lollapalooza, closures, parades) and 'City-level bus and rail demand' from the system table, lock before the first target day, and resolution at day 75 for CTA. It gives CTA lags of 40 to 59 days for Mar to Aug 2026.

assumptions: Rev 2, owner decisions (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08). Series: rail only. Bus and Divvy stay runners-up: Divvy for its 3-to-9-day lag (licence issues noted in evidence), bus as a possible second cell. Zero point: yoy(k=3, calendar=true, spread=rms12), formerly cal_yoy3 (G1). Rights: this overturns rev 1's recommendation to score from a private archive meanwhile. Scoring waits for maintainers to accept the terms reading and the indemnity clause, and the pilot may archive privately. Pilot: two unscored rounds (G3), because late fill-in and revisions were not measured directly. Only arrival dates were measured, from :created_at. The first scored lock moves from 2026-12-31 to 2027-02-28.

Question picked from the doc's eight. Regular-tier number: monthly rail boardings from the CTA system table. Reasons: the doc's own 'City-level bus and rail demand' row; the only series measurable here in one small request with 10 years of history; one number first (skill step 1). Runners-up: Divvy (kept as runner-up in rev 2); TNP pickups by community area, whose 3-minute aggregate timeout makes it the heaviest to run; the Lollapalooza joint profile, which is the event tier, for a later card once the regular adapter exists (Lollapalooza 2027 is in early August, so the lock would be about late July 2027).

Lesson 14 tests as written. Behavioral: pass (boardings). Spatial: pass (one transit system's use of the city; no geographic split in this number). Recurring: monthly and still updating, but the lag ranges from 40 to 150 days and months post out of order, so 'predictable schedule' is weak. That is noted, not grounds to reject. Public and archivable: free and keyless pass; archive terms are inferred (rights: permission-needed, rev 2). Prospective: pass (lock before the month). Scorable: pass.

The resolution is the first complete snapshot, not the doc's day 75. Reason: a fixed day 75 would have resolved 6 of the last 20 months before they posted. Runner-up: day 100 fixed. It is simpler, but it delays every round by weeks and still misses Jan and Feb 2025.

The holiday list is CTA's six observed holidays, fixed in the round text at lock. Reason: it matches every U-coded weekday since 2022. Runner-up: copy last year's day types onto the target month, which mishandles moving holidays.
Trend window: the three newest complete months in the lock capture. Reason: it is the same 3-month rule the doc uses for Texas. Runner-up: 6 months, which is steadier but lags more.
Daily fetch at 14:00 UTC with a 900-day window. It covers M-12, the spread's 12 past targets and their own year-earlier months (about M-28), plus the up-to-150-day lag.

Suggested arena names: tracker 'cta'; series 'cta_rail_monthly'; adapter ssa/adapters/cta_daily.py with a fetch_text/parse split; archive sources/cta_daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json; round_id 'cta-rail-<YYYY-MM>'; zero_point yoy(k=3, calendar=true, spread=rms12).
